This notebook follows the [analysis workflow](../3-workflow.md) step by step. Each numbered section matches a step in that guide. The notebook handles the coding. Your team makes the decisions, in chunks marked **You decide**.

Run chunks from top to bottom with the green play buttons, or click Knit to run everything.

## 0. Setup

Install packages once with `source("../../environment/install_r_packages.R")`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)

data_dir <- "../data"
results_dir <- "results"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

load_table <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path) || file.info(path)$size == 0) {
    message(basename(path), ": pending release (file is empty for now).")
    return(NULL)
  }
  read.csv(path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
}
```

## 1. Pick a Question

**You decide:** Our question is ...

## 2. Load and Check the Data

If a check prints `FALSE` or a nonzero duplicate count, note it in your analysis plan and tell an organizer. Do not edit the data files.

```{r load}
counts <- load_table(file.path(data_dir, "track01_counts_vt.csv"))
metadata <- load_table(file.path(data_dir, "track01_metadata_vt.csv"))

if (!is.null(counts) && !is.null(metadata)) {
  cat("Counts:", nrow(counts), "genes x", ncol(counts), "samples\n")
  cat("Metadata:", nrow(metadata), "samples x", ncol(metadata), "fields\n\n")
  cat("Samples in both tables:  ", length(intersect(colnames(counts), rownames(metadata))), "\n")
  cat("Counts are nonnegative:  ", all(as.matrix(counts) >= 0), "\n")
  cat("Counts are whole numbers:", all(as.matrix(counts) %% 1 == 0), "\n")
  cat("Duplicate genes:         ", sum(duplicated(rownames(counts))), "\n")
  cat("Duplicate samples:       ", sum(duplicated(colnames(counts))), "\n")
  # Put metadata rows in the same order as the count columns
  metadata <- metadata[colnames(counts), , drop = FALSE]
  print(data.frame(n_missing = colSums(is.na(metadata)),
                   n_unique = sapply(metadata, function(x) length(unique(x)))))
}
```

## 3. Explore the Samples

Change `color_by` to different metadata columns and rerun to see which fields line up with the main patterns.

```{r explore}
# You decide: a metadata column name to color the points by
color_by <- NULL

if (!is.null(counts)) {
  log_cpm <- log2(t(t(as.matrix(counts)) / colSums(counts)) * 1e6 + 1)
  pca <- prcomp(t(log_cpm))
  var_pct <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2))
  pcs <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2], sample = colnames(counts))
  pcs$color <- if (is.null(color_by)) "all" else metadata[[color_by]]
  ggplot(pcs, aes(PC1, PC2, color = color, label = sample)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_text(size = 2.5, vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", var_pct[1], "% of variation)"),
         y = paste0("PC2 (", var_pct[2], "% of variation)"),
         color = color_by, title = "Samples by overall gene activity") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## 4. Choose a Comparison

Use exact column names and values from the metadata. Write a short justification in your analysis plan.

```{r compare}
# You decide
group_column <- NULL   # e.g. "column_name"
case <- NULL           # e.g. "value_for_group_A"
control <- NULL        # e.g. "value_for_group_B"
covariates <- c()      # e.g. c("another_column")

comp_counts <- NULL
if (is.null(group_column) || is.null(case) || is.null(control)) {
  message("Fill in group_column, case and control above, then rerun this chunk.")
} else if (!is.null(counts)) {
  used <- c(group_column, covariates)
  comp_meta <- metadata[metadata[[group_column]] %in% c(case, control), used, drop = FALSE]
  n_before <- nrow(comp_meta)
  comp_meta <- comp_meta[complete.cases(comp_meta), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(comp_meta) < n_before) {
    message(n_before - nrow(comp_meta), " sample(s) dropped for missing values. Report this.")
  }
  comp_meta[[group_column]] <- relevel(factor(comp_meta[[group_column]]), ref = control)
  comp_counts <- as.matrix(counts[, rownames(comp_meta)])
  print(table(comp_meta[[group_column]]))
}
```

## 5. Run the Test

```{r deseq, message=FALSE}
res <- NULL
if (!is.null(comp_counts)) {
  design <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(c(covariates, group_column), collapse = " + ")))
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = comp_counts, colData = comp_meta, design = design)
  dds <- DESeq(dds)
  res <- as.data.frame(results(dds, contrast = c(group_column, case, control)))
  res <- res[order(res$padj), ]
  write.csv(res, file.path(results_dir, "de_results.csv"))
  head(res, 10)
}
```

## 6. Read the Results

`log2FoldChange` +1 means twice as high in case. `padj` is the adjusted p-value, smaller means stronger evidence. Set your own cutoffs and note how much the number of passing genes changes.

```{r results}
# You decide
padj_cutoff <- NULL   # e.g. a value between 0 and 1
lfc_cutoff <- NULL    # e.g. a minimum absolute log2 fold change, or 0

hits <- NULL
if (!is.null(res)) {
  plot_df <- res[!is.na(res$padj), ]
  plot_df$passing <- FALSE
  if (!is.null(padj_cutoff) && !is.null(lfc_cutoff)) {
    plot_df$passing <- plot_df$padj < padj_cutoff & abs(plot_df$log2FoldChange) >= lfc_cutoff
    hits <- plot_df[plot_df$passing, ]
    cat(nrow(hits), "genes pass\n")
    write.csv(hits, file.path(results_dir, "passing_genes.csv"))
  } else {
    message("Set padj_cutoff and lfc_cutoff to highlight genes.")
  }
  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), color = passing)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey75", `TRUE` = "firebrick")) +
    labs(x = paste("log2 fold change (", case, "vs", control, ")"),
         y = "-log10 adjusted p-value", title = "Volcano plot") +
    theme_minimal()
  ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "volcano.png"), p, dpi = 300, width = 7, height = 5)
  p
}
```

## 7. Connect Genes to Cell Types

Check which passing genes are broad cell-type markers, then look up at least three genes in the [Zeisel/Admati gene browser](https://storage.googleapis.com/www_zeisellab/PE_web/pe_web_test_v1.html) and record what you see.

```{r markers}
markers <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "interpretation", "track01_marker_matrix.csv"))
if (!is.null(hits)) {
  overlap <- merge(markers, data.frame(gene_symbol = rownames(hits), hits[, c("log2FoldChange", "padj")]))
  if (nrow(overlap) == 0) message("None of your passing genes are in the marker table.") else overlap
}

# You decide: one row per gene you looked up in the browser
browser_lookups <- data.frame(
  gene = character(), cell_types_expressing = character(),
  differs_PE_vs_control = character(), notes = character()
)
if (nrow(browser_lookups) > 0) write.csv(browser_lookups, file.path(results_dir, "browser_lookups.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 8. Optional: Single-Cell Extension

Filter the pseudobulk tables to one cell type, then rerun Sections 4 to 6 with them. Each donor counts once, and the early-onset comparison is exploratory.

```{r extension}
pb_counts <- load_table(file.path(data_dir, "extension", "pseudobulk", "track01_pseudobulk_counts.csv"))
pb_metadata <- load_table(file.path(data_dir, "extension", "pseudobulk", "track01_pseudobulk_metadata.csv"))
if (!is.null(pb_counts)) head(pb_metadata)
```
